data.rationale: uadd() assumes its second operand y is the larger one: its unrolled loop reads x->p[i] and y->p[i] for i < x->sz (line 353), the tail loop reads y->p[i] for i < y->sz, and it writes the final carry at z->p[y->sz] (line 401). Upstream mruby swaps x/y at the top of uadd so that x->sz >= y->sz; this variant lacks that normalization. mpz_add() (line 527) calls uadd(&z, x, y) at lines 614/618 with operands in arbitrary order, so when x->sz > y->sz the loops read past the end of y's limb buffer. Reproduced under ASan via the mruby_fuzzer target (LLVMFuzzerTestOneInput -> mrb_load_string -> mrb_bint_add -> mrb_bint_add_n -> mpz_add -> uadd): the input '666666666666 &6666...6666,6666...6666 +6666...6610000' builds two bigint literals of different limb counts and adds them, triggering 'READ of size 4 at 0 bytes after 40-byte region' in uadd at bigint.c:360. Fix: swap so the larger operand is y (or iterate over min/max sizes correctly).
